scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Both user LANs lost cross-AS connectivity this morning: pc1
(195.11.14.2) cannot reach pc2 (200.1.1.2) and pc2 cannot reach
pc1. Each PC still reaches its own gateway fine. Our NOC checked
router1: its inter-AS interface eth0 shows UP and its config is
unchanged. The partner operator (AS 2) says router2's logs show
the eBGP session dropping. Find what broke.

injection.action: administratively down the inter-AS interface (eth0) on router2

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router2 eth0 (193.10.11.2/24, the inter-AS
  interface toward router1)
Mechanism: router2's eth0 is DOWN, so the physical/L2 path between
  the two ASes is broken at router2's side. router2 immediately
  loses its 193.10.11.0/24 connected route and its BGP route to
  195.11.14.0/24 (nexthop interface gone), and its side of the
  eBGP session drops. Traffic from pc1 toward 200.1.1.0/24 is
  blackholed on the inter-AS segment (nothing listens at
  193.10.11.2 any more), so pc1<->pc2 fails in both directions.
  Note: router1's eth0 still shows UP (the far side of the virtual
  link keeps carrier), and router1 may briefly keep showing the
  session as Established until its hold timer expires -- the
  definitive evidence is router2's eth0 being DOWN.
Localization: router2
Root cause: inter-AS link down at router2 (eth0 administratively
  down)
Fix: `ip link set eth0 up` on router2
scenario.fix_spec:
Bring the inter-AS link back up: on router2 run `ip link set eth0 up`. The
eBGP session re-establishes, the inter-AS prefixes are re-exchanged, and pc1
reaches pc2 normally. router1 needs no change -- it was healthy the whole time.
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: inter-AS interface eth0 on router2 is down
must-identify-mechanism: the L2 path between the ASes is broken at router2's side, with the BGP session/route loss as a consequence
bonus-notes-far-side-up: notes router1's eth0 still shows UP (far side of the virtual link), so checking router1 alone would miss the fault

line.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

agent.diagnosis_text:
The eBGP session between AS 1 (router1) and AS 2 (router2) has
collapsed because router2's inter-AS interface eth0 is down. The
interface flags show only <BROADCAST,MULTICAST> with no UP or
LOWER_UP bits set, meaning the interface has no active link state.
Consequently, the 193.10.11.0/24 transit subnet is unreachable from
router2's side: a ping from router1 to 193.10.11.2 yields 100%
packet loss, and FRR itself reports "No path to specified Neighbor"
when attempting to establish the TCP/179 connection toward
193.10.11.1.

With the TCP session impossible to build, the eBGP finite-state
machine on router2 is stuck in the Active state (one established
session, one drop logged). Router2 therefore holds no route to
195.11.14.0/24, so traffic from pc2 (200.1.1.2) toward pc1
(195.11.14.2) is black-holed at router2. Router1's BGP process
still shows the session as recently up only because the 180-second
hold timer has not yet expired — it will transition to Idle
shortly.

Root cause: router2's eth0 (the inter-AS peering interface,
193.10.11.2/24) is operationally down, tearing down the eBGP
session and withdrawing cross-AS reachability.

Corrective fix: bring the interface back up on router2 with
`ip link set eth0 up`. The BGP session will re-establish within
one Connect-Retry interval (currently 61 seconds), prefixes will
be exchanged in both directions, and pc1 ↔ pc2 connectivity will
be restored.
